# Nextcloud brand string literals that are legitimate in fork test code.
#
# Each rule is an extended regex matched against "<path>|<literal>", so a rule
# can be brand-wide (match the literal alone) or pinned to one file (lead with
# the path). Every rule must carry a reason, and a rule that stops matching
# anything fails the scan so it gets pruned rather than quietly widening it.
#
# Before adding a rule, check the literal is not one the fork should own: a path
# segment, a data folder or a preferences filename belongs behind a runtime
# accessor (MainApp.getDataFolder(), getAuthority(), the package name), never in
# a string. See XNT-125, XNT-170 and XNT-194.

# Upstream hosts and the test accounts derived from them. These name
# Nextcloud's own servers and fixtures, not our product.
nextcloud\.(com|org|local|localhost|example\.com)

# The upstream community handle, asserted by CommunityFragmentIT against links
# that really do point at Nextcloud's social accounts.
[Nn]extclouders

# Test account names on a bare "nextcloud" realm, from upstream fixtures.
\|"[^"]*@nextcloud"

# SQL fixture rows carrying such an account name inside a longer CSV string.
'test@nextcloud'

# Fully-qualified upstream class names used as strings: reflection targets,
# mockk static targets and screenshot test-class names. A rename here breaks
# compilation elsewhere, so these cannot rot unnoticed.
#
# The trailing segment must be an uppercase-initial class name. Without that,
# "com.nextcloud.client_preferences.xml" — the XNT-194 literal itself — reads as
# a package path and this rule excuses the very thing the scan exists to catch.
\|"com\.nextcloud(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*"$

# The pre-rename data folder, named deliberately: this constant and this
# migration source path exist to recognise the old layout on disk.
datamodel/FileDataStorageManagerMigrateStoredFilesTest\.kt\|"/storage/emulated/0/Android/media/eu\.xeniacloud\.files/nextcloud"
client/migrations/DataFolderMigrationTest\.kt\|"nextcloud"

# Server-supplied notification payload text. NotificationsFragmentIT feeds the
# adapter a Notification exactly as a Nextcloud server sends it; the brand name
# is the server's wording, not a string this app owns.
ui/fragment/NotificationsFragmentIT\.kt\|"(Help improve Nextcloud|Do you want to help us to improve Nextcloud[^"]*)"

# Upstream task-app description text in a fixture app list.
"Sync tasks from various devices with your Nextcloud and edit them online\."

# A public-link fixture on an upstream test host, with an /owncloud/ path.
"https://nextcloud\.localhost/owncloud/[0-9a-z]+"
